open.name: The harbour
open.sub: the water street and its quays

locked.name: Sterncastle
locked.sees: Tall doors at the aft end of the main deck, barred from inside. The stern windows glow at night; the great wheel on the quarterdeck is lashed and never turns.

locked.name: Stern quarters
locked.sees: Doors off the harbour’s aft quays, and the galleries over the water with their shutters.

locked.name: Stern stores
locked.sees: Shuttered bays along the harbour’s aft quays.

locked.name: Timber store
locked.sees: Iron grilles on the port side of the Slip; stacked timber behind them.

locked.name: Warehouses
locked.sees: Barred doors along the harbour’s quays amidships.

locked.name: The Holds
locked.sees: Iron grilles along the forward quays; padlocked cargo hatches on the main deck.

locked.name: Purser’s stores
locked.sees: A door in the Tally House’s forward wall, by the pay booth.

locked.name: The Ropewalk
locked.sees: Double doors off the Well’s port gallery; the creak of a rope being laid.

locked.name: Mess and galley
locked.sees: A door off the Well’s forward gallery; the galley chimney smokes on the main deck.

locked.name: Guild rooms
locked.sees: Doors with painted crests off the Well’s aft gallery; their galleries over the harbour.

locked.name: Lantern Market
locked.sees: A rope across the forward gallery with a board: “Market closed”; light and voices behind shutters.

locked.name: Archive
locked.sees: A door with a brass plate off the Well’s aft gallery; its galleries high over the harbour.

locked.name: Inn and bunkrooms
locked.sees: A door off the forward gallery; laughter behind it in the evening.

locked.name: Forecastle
locked.sees: A barred door in the forecastle’s front beside the Chandlery, and one in the shop’s back wall; a gallery high over the shop.

locked.name: Forecastle deck and the head
locked.sees: Chained ladders up the forecastle’s front at both ends; the bowsprit and the beakhead beyond.

locked.name: Masts and tops
locked.sees: Shrouds whose ratlines start out of reach; the tops’ lanterns at night.

locked.name: The Deep
locked.sees: Under the waterline; no way down yet (D70: the Keelgate is out of the hub for now).

locked.name: Sail lofts and workshops
locked.sees: Doors off the Well’s gun-deck gallery; canvas and tar.

G1.name: Barred door
G1.why: Somebody’s room or business, not open to you yet.
G1.how: A timber door with an iron bar and a padlock. E: a short line of why.

G2.name: Rope and board
G2.why: Work going on, or closed for now.
G2.how: A rope across the way on stanchions (or between the door posts), a hand-painted board on it.

G3.name: Chained ladder or hatch
G3.why: Up or down: masts, forecastle, cargo hatches.
G3.how: A chain through the rungs or the grating, padlocked.

G4.name: Shutters
G4.why: Windows and bays of locked rooms.
G4.how: Closed shutters: nothing inside to see, nothing inside to build.

G5.name: Ancient seal
G5.why: The lost civilisation: the main quest.
G5.how: Pale seamless stone, turquoise lines, no handle, no lock.

G6.name: Iron grille
G6.how: Bars you see through into a shallow set, 2 to 3 m deep, and no further.
G6.line: Stacked timber, and no way in.

gate_marks.line: Barred from inside. The council meets here.

outside.hull_section: Planked all the way down (D64: no pale ancient band outside; the ancient hull shows only inside, in the Deep): flat bottom +/-6 m at the keel (z -12), +/-16 m at z -6, +/-19 m at the waterline, widest +/-20 m at z +6, tumblehome to +/-18.8 m at the main deck rail and +/-17.4 m at the taffrail. Fine at the ends below the water (hub.form): the run aft narrows to the sternpost, the entry forward is finer than the deck outline.
outside.stern: A galleon’s stern (D64, D69): the sterncastle rises in two tiers, the quarterdeck over x 24..48 (deck 22.5) and the poop over x 0..24 (three storeys, deck 28.5). Below the counter (z 8.5) the hull narrows to the sternpost and the one rudder; above it the stern is full width and round in plan, a half ellipse 9.5 m deep that runs into the sides without a corner, leaning aft a little. On its face: rows of tall cabin windows on each storey; grand open galleries at sc1 and sc2, 3.4 m deep, round the stern and along both sides to x 21.5, on carved brackets with balustrades and columns, the upper one roofed; glazed doors from the cabins onto them. Her name in carved brass letters under the taffrail, three great lanterns on the taffrail. The castles’ fronts are glazed in iron frames, with grand stairs along the bulwarks up to the quarterdeck and the poop; on the poop the command hall in glass under a copper roof. The tiller comes in through the counter; the lashed great wheel is on the quarterdeck.
outside.sides: Dark tarred planking in strakes about 0.55 m wide with a lively sheer (hub.sheer: up 2.2 m at the stern, 2.6 m at the stem); heavy wales in a belt at the waterline and at the deck lines, standing out like mouldings; ochre bands; lidded square ports (1 m) on every deck below the main deck down to the dock deck, cream-framed windows above it; most shut, some lit at night. Channels with deadeyes at each mast. The hidden doors (D70: four) at x 32..40 and 104..112 on both sides, from under the water to 13 m: shut, the planking, wales and painted port lids run on across them; only a seam and the iron hinge straps show.
outside.masts: x 68, 100, 140 (hub.rig in numbers); 54, 76, 64 m above the main deck; square yards on all three (D69: the mizzen’s lateen yard is gone); every sail furled on its yard, gathered canvas bound by gaskets; shrouds to the channels, stays forward, a long oxblood-and-cream pennant at the main truck.
outside.bow: Forecastle x 134..160, a storey over the main deck with a rail; a plain stem with two hawse holes and their cables to the anchors ahead; the beakhead out from the stem under the bowsprit (a grated platform, headrails curving up to the forecastle, a carved figurehead); the bowsprit from (154, 23.5) to (188, 30.5) with its spritsail yard, held down by its bobstay.
outside.colours: Hull planking dark tarred brown; ochre bands, muted; window frames cream; carvings and the name brass, muted; decks teak and its light and dark variants; canvas; iron.
